name: Royal Pavilion

dates.altered: Periodic restorations from the mid C19 to the late C20; an extensive programme of exterior restoration had just been completed at the time the entry was written, which it dates May 1992.
dates.note: The entry states 'The final phase began in February of 1811 under the architect James Wyatt' and 'Between 1814 and 1823, Nash gave the building the appearance which it has today', and separately says the decoration 'was completed by the summer of 1823'. The node's exemplar gives 1823 and 'Remodelled by Nash 1815-23'. Both are recorded; neither is resolved.

quotes.text: The final phase began in February of 1811 under the architect James Wyatt. Between 1814 and 1823, Nash gave the building the appearance which it has today. Periodic restorations from the mid C19 to the late C20.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1380680, Details, history paragraph

quotes.text: MATERIALS: stucco, scored to imitate ashlar; Bath stone and Portland stone dressings, recently renewed; the tent roofs and onion domes were originally surfaced with a patent mastic and painted to resemble Bath stone; the mastic failed in 1827 and was replaced by copper sheathing; various other roofs of slate.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1380680, Details, MATERIALS paragraph

quotes.text: EXTERIOR: East Front: composed of 5 distinct parts, symmetrically arranged around the 7-bay colonnade of the rotunda
quotes.page: Official list entry 1380680, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph; the extract cut this sentence mid-clause and it is quoted only as far as it was read

quotes.text: There are stacks with gathered flues symmetrically disposed across the roof; each flue is topped by a minaret-like chimney pot.

In 1817, Holland's angled bays were replaced by the box-like pavilions containing the Music and Banqueting Rooms. During the following summer Nash erected the great onion dome which dominates the east elevation and is flanked, to the west, by a pair of crenellated, oval towers. In 1819 the Bath stone window tracery and leaf columns were added
quotes.page: Official list entry 1380680, Details, history paragraph

quotes.text: range, with end pavilions similar to those already described, but flush with the intermediate range wall; 5-bay stone verandah projects from this wall and spans basement area.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. The entry runs to several thousand words and two extracts returned different spans of it; what came back is quoted and no span was joined to another. The node's exemplar calls the building 'structurally a cast-iron frame'; nothing in the spans read here says so, which is a silence and not a contradiction -- the entry's INTERIOR paragraphs, which were not returned, are where such a statement would sit.
